headline: Density is how much is packed into a space—and it applies to time, attention, and meaning too
universal_truth: Same volume, different content; what matters isn't just space but what fills it
fun_facts: A teaspoon of neutron star material weighs about 6 billion tons
Gold is about 19 times denser than water—that's why gold feels so heavy for its size
Air is about 1,000 times less dense than water, which is why we can walk through it easily
discussion_questions: Is your time densely or sparsely filled?
What areas of your life have high 'density' of meaning?
When is density good and when is it overwhelming?

hook.script: A basketball and a bowling ball are similar sizes, but wildly different weights. That's density—how much stuff is packed into a space. The same concept applies beyond physics: some hours are dense with meaning, others are sparse. Some conversations pack years of insight into minutes.

cliff.script: Density is about concentration—more in less space. This applies to information, experience, and value. How do we think about density in life, not just physics?

options.text: High density is valuable when you want maximum impact in limited space—concentrated effort, rich experiences, potent communication—but too much density overwhelms
options.response: Yes. Dense communication conveys more. Dense practice develops faster. But density has costs—it's harder to absorb, easier to miss details. The right density matches the situation.

options.text: More density is always better—efficiency means packing more in
options.response: Efficiency likes density, but absorption has limits—too dense and things get missed...

fact1.title: Physical Density
fact1.script: In physics, density is mass divided by volume. Same size, different weight means different density. This determines whether things float or sink, feel heavy or light for their size, and how materials behave.

fact2.title: Time Density
fact2.script: Some hours pack more living than others. A rich conversation, deep work, or peak experience has high 'temporal density'—more happens, more matters. Other hours pass without impact. Quality varies independent of quantity.

fact3.title: Information Density
fact3.script: A poem can be denser than a novel—more meaning per word. A formula can encode what takes paragraphs to explain. High information density requires more effort to unpack but communicates more efficiently.

wisdom.script: Here's today's wisdom: Same volume, different content. What matters isn't just space but what fills it. Seek density where it counts—rich experiences, potent work, meaningful time.

outro.script: That's Day 219. Tomorrow, we'll explore pressure—force spread over area. Until then, identify where you want more density in your life.

growTrack.title: Density Audit - Where's the Richness?
growTrack.learning_objective: Identify areas of high and low density
growTrack.activity: Where in your life is there high density—rich meaning, concentrated value, deep engagement? Where is there low density—empty time, sparse meaning? Can you shift some low-density areas toward higher density? Not more time, but more in the time.
